critical_negative_results.claim: A train/runtime representation mismatch was identified: a runtime KRAFTAUSDRUECKE block existed in the production prompt but was absent from 3785 training examples.
critical_negative_results.current_law: Every runtime-visible structural projection that the model must handle needs explicit train/eval coverage or a deliberate held-out generalization test; runtime format cannot be assumed from prose similarity.

critical_negative_results.claim: v26.1 max_len=1408 reportedly truncated 2907/3785 examples (76.8%), discarding about 1,023,224 tokens from the left, including early identity/system sections.
critical_negative_results.current_law: Before paid Clay training, mechanically render the exact final corpus and prove zero unintended truncation of mandatory semantic fields at the selected context length.

critical_negative_results.claim: The project discovered after v26.1 training that the nominal eval file had not been consumed by the training scripts; an actual 328-case runtime-format evaluator was built only afterward.
critical_negative_results.current_law: Dataset existence != evaluation execution. Final training jobs require executable receipts proving eval_dataset attachment, periodic eval, final held-out inference and artifact identity.

critical_negative_results.claim: Historical tool-reference data contained ambiguous/wrong labels (e.g. similar system_check/body or calendar/calendar_add semantics), producing symmetric confusions that could be data-quality rather than model-reasoning failures.
critical_negative_results.current_law: Evaluation/training labels must be semantically discriminative and audited before interpreting model errors; label ambiguity is its own error class.

critical_negative_results.claim: Historical version numbering/artifact location was inconsistent: training-suite notes observed live v25 while the mapped laptop's newest visible adapter was v23, with uncertainty about where v24/v25 were trained.
critical_negative_results.current_law: Model/base/adapter/corpus/runtime identity must be content-addressed and provenance-bound; human version labels are display metadata, not identity.

REUSE: QLoRA/PEFT adapter training and compact runtime-adapter deployment pattern

ADAPT: Old personality and self-model data can inform corpus structure but must be rewritten for the current FRANK/Q12/Clay architecture and current owner directives.
Historical GWT/body/state blocks are templates for state-conditioned learning, not current canonical field definitions.
Historical runtime/eval scripts are method references; current Together/local target requires new provider-specific receipts and current Clay semantics.
SUPERSEDE: Do not train old tool-selection behavior into the Clay model: current owner-fixed architecture assigns tool use completely to Needle.
Do not train fixed hardware/API quotas or other live values as model knowledge; these remain dynamic state/tool outputs.
Do not inherit old room/world metaphors, internal module names or superseded prompt projections as mandatory Clay semantics.
Do not copy old natural-language/JSON/tag representations when Clay is now the native semantic language.
NEW_TARGET: goal formation/revision under the current safe-effect architecture
current Needle boundary understanding without model-authored tool authority

branch_feedback.hyperposition: Train relation/topology semantics only from current explicit higher-order contracts and controls, not quantum-like analogy language.
branch_feedback.unifieddb: Corpus source identity, trainability eligibility, version/supersession and model artifact lineage require durable provenance state.
